title: CO2 was taught as categorically useless against a lithium battery fire, with an operational conclusion to withhold the fixed system, and a ro-ro passenger circular was cited as generic containership guidance
candidate_claim: Founder/GPT independent high-risk review. QB2_A#q7 teaches that 'CO2 will not extinguish a Li-ion thermal runaway' and derives an operational conclusion equivalent to 'do not release / do not waste the fixed CO2 system'. That conflates the self-sustaining internal reaction with oxygen-dependent flaming combustion in an enclosed space. The same card's REG-BOX cites MSC.1/Circ.1615 as though it were IMO guidance specifically governing a containerized lithium battery fire.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD ON BOTH, AND THE FIRST IS THE MOST SAFETY-SENSITIVE ITEM IN THE TRANCHE. The card was RIGHT that CO2 cannot cool the cells or terminate thermal runaway, and that limb is preserved verbatim in substance. It was WRONG to convert that into 'CO2 will not extinguish' plus 'releasing CO2 can waste your fixed extinguishing agent', because a fixed gaseous installation in an enclosed protected space addresses exactly the oxygen-dependent flaming combustion that a battery fire also produces, and telling a Chief Engineer to hold back an installed system because lithium is involved is unsafe advice in an oral he may one day act on. The old answer was also a UNIVERSAL action sequence with no reference to location, accessibility, whether the space is enclosed, what is installed, or the Master's command.

authority.co2_position: Two distinct mechanisms, and the corrected card states both. (A) THERMAL RUNAWAY: CO2 removes no heat from the cells, does not stop the internal electrochemical self-heating, and cannot by itself prevent propagation or re-ignition - so cooling is crucial. (B) FLAMING COMBUSTION IN AN ENCLOSED SPACE: this is oxygen-dependent and is what a fixed gaseous system in a protected space is for. The oral answer the review directed, and which the card now carries in substance, is: CO2 may suppress the external flaming fire, but it cannot cool the battery or terminate internal thermal runaway; re-ignition and continued propagation remain possible, so the fixed-system response must be combined with temperature monitoring, boundary cooling and the ship's emergency procedure.
authority.release_decision: Release of a fixed extinguishing system is a decision for the Master under the ship's fire control plan and emergency procedure, on the Chief Engineer's technical advice. What decides it is the location and accessibility of the fire, whether the space is enclosed and can be sealed, whether anybody is unaccounted for inside, and what is actually installed - not the presence of lithium cells. The card no longer instructs the candidate to withhold an installed system.
authority.cooling_distinction: External / boundary cooling and direct cell cooling are now distinguished wherever cooling is mentioned. For a closed container stowed in a hold only the boundary is reachable; direct cooling of the cells is available only where the pack is accessible. This is consistent with, and was already stated by, the card's own AVD section, which was examined and left intact.
authority.msc1_circ_1615_actual_scope: MSC.1/Circ.1615 is 'Interim guidelines for minimizing the incidence and consequences of fires in ro-ro spaces and special category spaces of new and existing ro-ro passenger ships', approved at MSC 101 and dated 26 June 2019. It carries material on alternatively powered vehicles. It is NOT generic containership or containerized-lithium-battery fire guidance.
authority.msc1_circ_1615_evidence_tier: STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. The circular itself is NOT HELD in the corpus, and IMO's own CDN path for it returned HTTP 404 when tried on 2026-09-04. The title, date and MSC 101 approval were confirmed against TWO INDEPENDENT SECONDARY SOURCES - the imorules.com circular index and Bureau Veritas's MSC 101 report - and they agree with the Founder/GPT independent verification. That is sufficient to establish that the card's old description was WRONG. It is NOT relied on for anything the circular SAYS, and the card asserts nothing about its content beyond its title and its scope.
authority.msc1_circ_1615_treatment: The review permitted removal, or retention 'only if the answer explicitly and accurately labels its ro-ro-passenger-space scope, which is probably unnecessary here'. RETENTION WITH AN EXPLICIT SCOPE LABEL WAS CHOSEN, as a row headed 'Scope caution - MSC.1/Circ.1615' that gives the real title, records that an earlier version of this card mis-cited it, and says in terms that it must not be quoted as generic containership guidance. The reasoning: this is a mis-citation the corpus itself made and that candidates repeat, so an inoculation is worth more than a silent deletion. NO SUBSTITUTE CIRCULAR WAS INVENTED. The choice is recorded here because it is a deviation from the review's stated preference and must be visible rather than inferred.
authority.imdg_separation: IMDG material kept and SEPARATED from firefighting guidance, as the review directed. One row now carries the TRANSPORT classification - Class 9, UN 3480 and UN 3481 as applicable to the consignment - and says in terms that it governs declaration, packing, marking, stowage and segregation and is not shipboard firefighting guidance. A second row carries the EmS emergency schedules F-A and S-I, qualified as 'shown against the applicable UN entry in the IMDG amendment in force', with the candidate told to read the entry for the consignment actually carried rather than a remembered pair. The pair F-A / S-I is NOT asserted here as verified against a held current IMDG entry; the qualification is what carries it.
